Jūlius, Jūlia, Jūlium

adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis), declension

of July; July

Named after Julius Caesar, who accepted a month named after himself (Suet. Jul. 76.1); before that it was Quīntīlis. Kalendae, Nōnae, Īdūs Jūliae: the 1st, 7th and 15th.

Other words

  • 1Quīntīlis: long first i (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). From quīntus. De Vaan 509, s.v. quīnque: the vowel of the ordinal was lengthened before the spirantized k (*kwīxto- > quīntus), and the long ī spread to quīnque. Traupman 78 marks Quīntīlis. Ruling: Which authority settles a vowel.

    Quīntīlis1, Quīntīle — July (the old name)

    adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis), declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.12.1: mēnse Quīntīlī; Liv. 9.46 (Īdibus Quīntīlibus, Lewis & Short); Traupman 78

    The fifth month, counting from March (quīntus; Varro, LL 6.34).

Examples

  • Jūliō mēnse, quō maximē lītēs interquiēscunt

    in July, when the lawcourts are at their quietestPlin. Ep. 8.21.2

  • negōtium magnum est nāvigāre atque id mēnse Quīntīlī

    sailing is hard work, and in July at thatCic. Att. 5.12.1

  • mēnse Jūliō

    in JulyTraupman 335

See also month, June, August, summer.
